events.description: * WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Kent MD. * WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to midnight EST Friday night. * IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels could reach near moderate flood stage during the Thursday evening high tide.

location.region: Kent

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 5:14AM EST until November 28 at 12:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to midnight EST Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels could reach near moderate flood
stage during the Thursday evening high tide.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
weather.areaDesc: Kent

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 1:54PM EST until November 28 at 12:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Thursday to midnight EST Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels could reach near moderate
flood stage during the Thursday evening high tide.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Thursday to 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers (including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact Ventura and Channel Islands Harbors. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of around 8.1 feet will peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.

location.region: Ventura County Beaches

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time

Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures.
Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and
strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean

(including Ventura Pier) and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Large breaking waves may impact

infrastructure.

closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.5 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. F For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft expected. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying

Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of

weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.description: ...The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in North Carolina... Northeast Cape Fear River Near Burgaw affecting Pender County. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Northeast Cape Fear River near Burgaw. * WHEN...From Friday morning to late Monday night. * IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Flooding worsens in the River Bend, River Birch and Alligator Lake subdivisions. Flooding on Croomsbridge RD and Old Maple Hill RD worsens and the roads may be impassable in multiple locations. Holly Shelter Estates begins to flood and flooding in Sandy Bend worsens. Flooding worsens near the ends of Turtle Hill TR, Hickory Hill LN, White Tail LN, Mallard Roost DR, and Oxbow Landing. Shaw Hwy is flooded at Ashes and Lillington Creeks. Equine Landing RD area may flood. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 4.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late tomorrow morning to a crest of 11.6 feet early Saturday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning. - Flood stage is 10.0 feet. - weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in North Carolina...

Northeast Cape Fear River Near Burgaw affecting Pender County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Northeast Cape Fear River near Burgaw.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Flooding worsens in the River Bend, River
Birch and Alligator Lake subdivisions. Flooding on Croomsbridge RD
and Old Maple Hill RD worsens and the roads may be impassable in
multiple locations.  Holly Shelter Estates begins to flood and
flooding in Sandy Bend worsens.  Flooding worsens near the ends of
Turtle Hill TR, Hickory Hill LN, White Tail LN, Mallard Roost DR,
and Oxbow Landing.  Shaw Hwy is flooded at Ashes and Lillington
Creeks. Equine Landing RD area may flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tomorrow morning to a crest of 11.6 feet early Saturday
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Monday
morning.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov/wfo/ilm .

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM EST.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM PST Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

weather.instruction:

wearing protective breathing masks if outside. High dust

problems, especially with children, elderly or those with
pre-existing respiratory conditions.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.4 feet will peak near 11 AM Friday morning.

weather.description:

For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15
feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.4
feet will peak near 11 AM Friday morning.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft. * WHERE...The Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 1:31AM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft.

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday
morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft. * WHERE...The Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Saturday morning. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 27 at 4:06PM EST until November 28 at 12:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Kent MD.

* WHEN...Until midnight EST tonight.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected. * WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

weather.description:

Washington...

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM PST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage early tomorrow

- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.1
feet on 12/15/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM PST.

events.description: * WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...In Delaware, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. In New Jersey, Ocean and Coastal Ocean. * WHEN...Until 4 AM EST Saturday. * IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Although no additional tidal flooding is expected on the oceanfront and Delaware Bay, flooding will linger on back bays including Barnegat, Rehoboth, and Little Assawoman Bays for the next several hours.

location.region: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches; Ocean; Coastal Ocean

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 27 at 9:56PM EST until November 28 at 4:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Delaware, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. In
New Jersey, Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in bayside communities and along tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Although no additional tidal flooding is
expected on the oceanfront and Delaware Bay, flooding will
linger on back bays including Barnegat, Rehoboth, and Little

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
weather.areaDesc: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches; Ocean; Coastal Ocean

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Ventura County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An abnormally high tide of around 7.2 feet will peak between 11 AM and Noon Saturday morning.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. Some
locations will experience zero visibility for several hours. This
dense fog event will be a Level 4 on a scale of 1 to 5.

* WHERE...Much of central California.

* WHEN...From 8 PM this evening to Noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dense fog will make driving conditions hazardous leading

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Dense fog will resemble that of the past two

sunset. Be aware that dense fog will be widespread by late this
evening, if you are traveling.

of distance ahead of you. Consider leaving after the dense fog has
gone. Be sure to change your headlights from AUTO to MANUAL, since
automatic headlights will not activate in the dense fog.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current. * WHERE...Northern to eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra. * WHEN...Through Sunday morning. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 27 at 6:59PM AST until November 29 at 8:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Northern to eastern beaches of Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.
weather.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft. * WHERE...The Pacific Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 6 AM Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM
Saturday, and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM
Sunday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
